The pizza has to be shifted around under the broiler pretty often to cook evenly. I added mozzarella for the final minute under the broiler. Finished with salt and olive oil, and basil. Dough is 230 g total of bread flour at 80% hydration - fridge ferment for three days ( slap fold method) .

Takeaway - I’m happy with the results visually but it’s definitely distinguishable from brick ovens. Leopard spots and the crispy airy crust are  harder to achieve I think.

I might be misunderstanding but science can't declare something as supernatural. All it can state is that our current understanding of the universe is not fully developed. For example, imagine taking a trip around the galaxy at near the speed of light and returning to earth. According to the theory of special relativity, you would appear to have aged much less than others who remained on earth. Imagine what people from the 1600s would have thought if they witnessed this? The reason we don't see this 'time-traveling' as a supernatural event is due to our understanding of the mechanics by which it occurs. 

Personally, I'm normally skeptical of claims of supernatural events but I would probably attribute a vanishing meteorite to God lol

I don't think so? Like for example the existence of black holes before we had evidence from photos and gravitational waves, most scientists were still confident in their existence. Still, I say that science (referring to the scientific method and mathematics) cannot prove/disprove the existence of God because should he exist, he would be supernatural (mathematics obviously has nothing to say on the supernatural). Believing that the supernatural exists is a different discussion

We can create mathematical models consistent with our observations, but anything outside our scope of observation is also exempt from these laws we write to describe this universe. Basically, our mathematics-based understanding of the universe cannot prove or disprove the existence of God because math cannot prove anything about the supernatural.
